The *Dhajadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 345) is a canonical Pali verse narrative preserved in the Therāpadāna collection of the Sutta Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Belonging to the biographical apadāna genre, the poem commemorates the deeds and past meritorious actions of the elder (thera) Dhajadāyaka. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text across five languages [SuttaCentral].
Computational analysis by DharmaNexus identifies substantial formulaic text reuse between this work and the broader Pali corpus, registering 76 matching passages across 20 distinct texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest textual relationship is with the Theragāthā commentary (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo), which shares 22 matching segments (spanning over 2,100 characters, most notably segments §2.1–4.2 aligning with §409–414), alongside further overlaps in its second section (*Dutiyo bhāgo*) [DharmaNexus]. Numerous verses are likewise shared internally within the Therāpadāna, prominently with texts such as the *Ukkhittapadumiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 342), *Subhūtittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 23), *Sakosakakoraṇḍadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 356), and *Sucintitattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 430) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, automated cross-linguistic alignment links portions of the text to the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* as well as the Tibetan translation of the *Vinayavastu* and the *Ārya-candrottarādārikāvyākaraṇa-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra* [DharmaNexus].
